Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours.
→ 15° per hour
→ 1° every 4 minutes
Crossing west adds a day; crossing east subtracts a day.
This forms the basis of local time and standard time.

items: 1° of longitude change corresponds strictly to a 4-minute time difference.
Crossing the International Date Line (180° longitude) Westwards ADDS a day, whereas Eastwards SUBTRACTS a day.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours, which translates to 15° per hour or 1° every 4 minutes.
The rotation of the Earth forms the basis of local time and standard time.
The International Date Line is located near 180° longitude.
Crossing the International Date Line to the west adds a day, while crossing to the east subtracts a day.

blocks.content: Located near 180° longitude. Crossing west adds a day; crossing east subtracts a day.
